# GOCOMMAND names the go command that a program reaches go/build through when
# GOROOT holds no bin/go. The go command writes the variable itself, and writes
# a path to its own executable, so a value that a PATH search would have to
# resolve did not come from this toolchain. go/build refuses such a value
# instead of running whichever go a shell has first, which is the lookup that
# naming the command was meant to avoid.

[short] skip 'builds and runs a program'

mkdir $WORK/fakeroot/src

# A go of someone else's on PATH, which must not run.
chmod 0777 fakebin/go
env PATH=$WORK/gopath/src/fakebin${:}$PATH

env FAKEGOROOT=$WORK/fakeroot
env SRCDIR=$WORK/gopath/src
env MARKER=$WORK/ran

# The go command writes GOCOMMAND itself for the programs it starts, so the
# program is built here and started from this script instead, the way a shell
# starts it with an environment of its own.
exec $GOROOT/bin/go build -o $WORK/gocommand$GOEXE gocommand.go
env GOCOMMAND=go
exec $WORK/gocommand$GOEXE
stdout 'is not an absolute path'
stdout 'refused without running the command'
! exists $WORK/ran

-- go.mod --
module gocommand

go 1.27
-- fakebin/go --
#!/bin/sh
echo ran > "$MARKER"
exit 0
-- gocommand.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"go/build"
	"os"
)

func main() {
	ctxt := build.Default
	ctxt.GOROOT = os.Getenv("FAKEGOROOT")

	_, err := ctxt.Import("example.com/absent", os.Getenv("SRCDIR"), 0)
	if err == nil {
		fmt.Println("BAD: Import succeeded")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println("import error:", err)

	if _, statErr := os.Stat(os.Getenv("MARKER")); statErr == nil {
		fmt.Println("BAD: GOCOMMAND was executed")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println("refused without running the command")
}
